claims.text: Nanostructured thin-film processing increases free-surface area relative to the bulk-like baseline.
Nanostructured thin-film processing increases grain-boundary density.
Grain boundaries and free surfaces mediate elastic accommodation during the magnetostructural transition.
Interfacial strain-energy barriers are responsible for the sharp transition in as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys.
Interfacial strain-energy barriers are responsible for hysteresis in as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys.
The bulk-like baseline has an ordered single-phase hexagonal structure.
The bulk-like baseline undergoes a first-order magnetostructural transition.
The baseline transition produces a large magnetocaloric response.
The baseline magnetocaloric response is hysteretic.
Increasing free-surface and grain-boundary density alleviates elastic constraints during the magnetostructural transition.
Free surfaces and grain boundaries reduce strain-energy barriers during the phase change.
Reducing strain-energy barriers lowers transition hysteresis.
Reducing strain-energy barriers produces a broader and smoother transition profile.
A higher surface-to-volume ratio facilitates faster heat exchange.
Nanostructured thin films should exhibit reduced hysteresis relative to the bulk-like baseline.
Nanostructured thin films should exhibit a less abrupt and smoother entropy change relative to the baseline.
Nanostructured thin films may exhibit a higher heat-exchange rate than the baseline.
The predicted effects require retention of the phase-pure hexagonal state without deleterious secondary phases.
The predicted effects should be most pronounced under low applied magnetic fields.
The predicted effects should be most pronounced when the transition temperature is near the operating range of the refrigeration cycle.

contradictions.description: The baseline is repeatedly called 'as-deposited' while being identified as arc-melted ingots or melt-spun microribbons. This conflates deposited material with materials made by melting or melt spinning and leaves the actual baseline processing state ambiguous.
